problems.desc: Part (b): the student says what went wrong in the subtraction that produced 44. Full credit for naming the flipped ones column: there were only three ones to take seven from, so instead of regrouping, the smaller digit was taken from the larger one and the column was worked backwards. Accept an answer that says a ten should have been opened into ten ones first, leaving five tens and thirteen ones. Half credit for saying only that the answer is too big, or that regrouping was needed, without saying which column was reversed. No credit for restating the correct difference, since part (a) already asks for it.

traps.desc: rounded the number being taken away down instead of up

problems.desc: Part (c): the student says why the estimate came out below the exact difference. Full credit for the idea that the number being taken away was rounded up while the number in front was rounded down, so more was taken away in the estimate than in the real subtraction, which pushes the estimate low. Accept an answer that tracks just one of the two roundings correctly and says which way it moved the result. Half credit for noticing only that the estimate is smaller, with no reason. No credit for claiming the estimate must always match the exact answer.
